title: nbn FTTP or HFC 500/50 $79.99/M, 750/50 $89.99/M, 1000/100 $99.99/M for 24 Months | eero 7 Router $99 + $10 Delivery @ Arctel
body:
Deal: nbn FTTP or HFC 500/50 $79.99/M, 750/50 $89.99/M, 1000/100 $99.99/M for 24 Months | eero 7 Router $99 + $10 Delivery @ Arctel

[Rorku] I’m paying $60 a month for 500/50 and not locked in for 2 whole years straight, doesn’t look like a deal to me
[FuRyZ] You underestimate who you are talking to. This is OzBargain not OzAdvertising.
Your deal sucks. Try harder or go somewhere else.
I literally just signed up for $50/month for 500/50 with Amaysim for 6 months and I damn well will be churning to the next best deal when those 6 months are up. I havent paid more than $60/month for internet in years and I have no plans on breaking that streak.
For those actually looking for a good deal, go here: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/970523
[Team Triforce] This deal is definitely not for everyone, doesn’t mean it’s not a good price.
SL & Aussie have some of the highest prices in market, also with the most subscribers?
Appreciate you dropping last though 👍🏽
[Fooah] You arent locked in, it's just the price that is.
[Team Triforce] Correct, we are locking in the price! You are free to leave at the end of any billing cycle.
[Team Triforce] We use a combination of Superloop & Vocus, backed by our own internet gateway.
[eddyah] I'm on a crap amaysim plan that my wife complains about poor speeds all the time (accessing asian content)
[Team Triforce] Well it’s a resold Optus service, shouldn’t be getting poor speeds from a provider like that. Issue is Amaysim only has limited control to support your service.
[CanolaRevolver] Hmm these aren’t great prices. The standard price for Amaysim NBN is the same as your discount price.
[Team Triforce] The wholesale cost for 500/50 NBN is over $50, which is why the on-going price from Amaysim is $90!
You would have noticed most providers are increasing their on-going pricing & reducing the upfront discounts.
If you are happy moving every 6-months, this is not the promotion for you.
[Team Triforce] Current POP's are NSW, VIC & WA. QLD is next to go live, followed by SA.
[Team Triforce] Pending IP allocation from APNIC… has been a long wait. We are exploring other alternatives for additional ranges, to enable peering. It is top of our list to resolve for our growing base of QLD customers.
[Team Triforce] SA is probably 2-3 months out, currently routing via VIC, this is about 10ms… however as there is no internet exit in SA anyway, outside of domestic traffic is routing back to VIC anyway!
[Fooah] Went with More telecom through commbank… $100 1000/200 for 36months. Might be worth for other ozbs who want the extra vibe for 3 years.
[Fooah] Couldnt tell you Commbanks interest rate, I dont owe them any money or pay any fees. Interesting assumption though.
[jv] $100 1000/200 for 36months.
they don't offer 1000/200
[internet-stranger] Your Critical Information Summary pricing does not match your site pricing.
Also CG-NAT or $5 for static IP.
[Team Triforce] Will check in here, the team has just launched a new look & link might be expired!
CG-NAT/Static info added.
Cheers.
[Team Triforce] Unfortunately not at present, we are struggling as it is with our allocation of public IP addresses… it’s something high on the agenda.
Would this make it a winner for you?
[IndianWarrior] I would say please avoid Arctel.
Had been struggling with frequent drop outs and they keep blaming NBN for that.
They don't have any thing through which they can check dropouts.
[Team Triforce] @IndianWarrior - Send through your request ID & can escalate with the team.
Overall, we have very few customers un-happy with the performance, our network is un-capped speed profiles, allowing you to use the maximum speed available.
The overall network is supporting 10's of thousands of customers, so if this was an issue it would have been resolved.
Here to help, shoot me a DM.
[askbargain] How many unplanned interruptions has Arctel had in the last month?
[Team Triforce] We also have direct access to all the tools the NBN provide… but once you send through your case, we will have a look into it for you more closely.
[BatmanAU] I agree, been with them a few weeks and speeds are average at best, even in their off peak times i get about 380-420meg on a 500 plan. When doing speed tests i keep picking up NSW end points and im nowhere near NSW. Pity i cant go back to my original ISP, time to shop around in 29 days
[Team Triforce] Hi Mate,
Drop a ticket through to support & DM me a #. Probably need a port reset, depending on your technology type.
Definitely shouldn’t be having an issue.
Thanks,
H
[Wiadro] Arctel, has its ips blocked by so many sites.
Carsales
eBay
gumtree
News com au
I would avoid all together, it will also take 2 hours to answer the phone if you have any issues
Also it will drop packets so sites don’t load.
The competitions are ALL bullshit.
[askbargain] Definitely not the case
??? You're reusing data centre IP's for residential customers and think nothing will go wrong
[Team Triforce] Where would you like us to get the IP's from if not within a DC? :o
[askbargain] @Team Triforce: I'm calling your bs on "Definitely not the case" which you don't seem to be disputing anymore
[Team Triforce] @askbargain: Would you like to explain to us how CG-NAT & hosted ranges work then?
All IP addresses are hosted in a data centre, but I’m all ears on how you think it works 👍🏽
[yak] @Team Triforce: You’re being disrespectful and disingenuous to @askbargain and trying to bamboozle or deceive regular Ozbargainers who don’t know better.
You’re splitting hairs on technical definitions to sow doubt and confusion while tryng to avoid base truths.
Advertise honestly or get out.
[Team Triforce] @yak: Question has no technical merit, we are an established provider & everything advertised is correct.
[yak] @Team Triforce: Are your IP blocks classified by 3rd parties as “residential”?
If the two Ozbargainers who explained their problems with your service are wrong then publish all of your IPv4 & 6 blocks so that anyone here can check them against an ASN database.
Don’t yell louder. Bring verifiable facts. Be honest. You’ve behaved like a snake oil salesman in this chat. Your behaviour is losing trust.
[howcan] What's a data centre IP? Can you explain what you think that is?
[askbargain] @howcan: Big company rate IP on risk. Categorise IP if risky. Big man Arctel have IP's previously used for hosting. Now use for NBN. Carsales, eBay etc. no like. They scared. IP's used for hosting scary.
Can you explain what you think that is?
[Team Triforce] @askbargain: Not true at all, we have multiple AS #’s & the IP addresses used for consumer NBN services do not have active hosting.
Once we assign a static IP address to an end-user, we can’t control what they do with it (including hosting their own server).
[askbargain] @Team Triforce: Just answer this: Are your consumer NBN IP ranges repurposed from your cloud hosting company?
[Team Triforce] @askbargain: No, they are independent ranges on seperate AS#’s as explained multiple times.
This is all public ally available information, you can verify it yourself if you don’t believe us.
[askbargain] @Team Triforce: Then why is your consumer IP ASN "DataKnox"? You're telling me these have been reserved and never used?
[Team Triforce] @askbargain: This is our core network service, we route all traffic out via our core network which allows us to balance the traffic between multiple state gateways.
Our hosting business also peers with this network, but has its own IP ranges. Every carrier works under the same model, to aggregate our total upstream capacity.
Happy to explain how the network works, here to help mate.
[askbargain] @Team Triforce: https://mxtoolbox.com/SuperTool.aspx?action=a%3amailout1.neo…
I wonder why this company would be using one of the IP's on your NBN range.
[Wiadro] @askbargain: yeah they are risky IP's
I couldn't buy anything from JB or TGG Commercial at home because it would take my money and then cancel the sale 5 min later and refund me.
also i had a static IP and not CG-NAT, so your once again bullshitting us.
your IP's are all rubbish, they dont allow the internet to be used like the internet.
[askbargain] @Wiadro: Watch out, he might blame you for making it risky!
[Wiadro] @askbargain: LOL, honestly, they did blame me for not having an Eero 7 (standard) modem, because I had an Eero 7 Pro, which is rubbish anyway, but it looks "nice" according to the mrs.
These are the speeds I got with Arctel back in October 2025, on a static IP 1000/100 plan
https://www.speedtest.net/result/18404575560
https://www.speedtest.net/result/18404575560
The moment I churned back to SL, my speeds were back to normal.
[yak] They’re using DC IPs? Yowch! You’d get blocked by websites or hit a Cloudflare “are you human?” check waaaaay more often than through a residential IP.
That’s all the drawbacks of using a commercial VPN without the benefits.
[Team Triforce] @yak: There is no merit to the conversation, IP’s are blacklisted based on bad usage - unfortunately we have users doing all sorts of things with their internet service.
When one of these users are on CG-NAT, they can impact the reputation of the outbound IP.
This is the reason we rotate the pool.
[yak] @Team Triforce: You aren't unique. AussieBroadband also has CGNAT. AussieBroadband also has customers that misbehave. But their IP ranges (and both ASNs) are published. Their customers don't have the same rate of IPs with bad reputations that your customers seem to suffer from. Just compare ABB's threads on OzB and Whirlpool to yours here.
So, blaming bad users and CGNAT doesn't stack up when ABB (and other ISPs) are a huge counterpoint.
There is no merit to the conversation
Sure there is. You could publish your IPv4/6 blocks and we could see their reputation for ourselves. You'd be vindicated. That would shut us all up.
[hmac] @yak: Commenting to downvote based on what I just read above.
But more importantly rep posted this on the previous deal today
20 August update : Free eero 7 router is now only included on 500/50, 750/50 and 1000/100
But it didn't appear to work on the website, so I called up their customer service to speak with them. Over 20 minutes, could not find my address, yet I can search it on their website and select a plan? Silence for over 5 minutes at a time where I need to check if they are still there. Cannot recommend based on my experiences alone. I opted for another provider
I did report the previous deal to have that removed so other people weren't misled or wasted their time, but store rep still hasn't responded to the comments on that thread posted well before this deal, too busy arguing with others here.
[Spizz] @yak: https://forums.whirlpool.net.au/thread/9kppyrnn
they are doing internal NAT switching to a private IP on your router rather than assigning a true, direct public static IP to your WAN port. Seems this unconventional way has some issues.
[seanbaussie] Throwing in a final run of eero 7's at $99
Then why does the title say $129?
[Team Triforce] Been a long day… I’ll cop that one! You signing up? I’ll throw you a eero for $50 for spotting the error 😎
[askbargain] ARCTEL provides a DDoS protected internet gateway
Interesting approach to sell CG-NAT.
[Team Triforce] Oh no… picking up another topic you don’t understand.
CG-NAT & in-line DDoS have nothing to do with eachother… but I’m holding my breath!
[yak] CGNAT already provides a basic level of DDOS. What magic sauce are you guys adding to it?
If we pay for a static IP then what DDOS protection remains and how effective is it? Can I run a self-hosted website through it without fear of DDOS or will I still need to pay Cloudflare for real DDOS protection?
[Team Triforce] Agreed, it does. All in-bound traffic is passed through an in-line scrubbing device, which provides protection to all of our hosted prefixes.
This is not sold as a SLA guaranteed service to consumer NBN services, but our transit gateways are shared between the enterprise & consumer network.
This is designed to be a value add service to our consumer customers.
[yak] @Team Triforce: That is neat. You should've led with the technical details, frankly, instead of being condescending and dismissive. @askbargain wasn't the only one with the question, he was just the first one to voice it. Many of us onlookers are interested in the informative answer and instead you answered his cynicism with verbal attacks. @askbargain wasn't out of line, because CGNAT could be described as "DDoS protected internet gateway" by an unscrupulous marketer.
The technical details of an inline DDOS scrubber (I assume that it reactively drops suspect packets from IPs that are hammering for too long (or is it getting info from 3rd party services?)) that hopefully doesn't add much latency to incoming traffic is the sort of cool feature that you should be taking advantage of @askbargain's comment to crow about.
You've been sabotaged by your own foul attitude.
Does the DDOS scrubber run on outbound traffic too, to stop your compromised/naughty customers from DDOS'ing others, or is it just inbound?
[HappyPants] I am a happy churner, so no deal for me. And I don't think I am alone…. it's not like changing providers every 6 months is hard yakka…and the best deals are always easy to find thanks to Ozbargain.
[Team Triforce] Completely respect your honesty, the only thing is the fact that half these deals are loss leaders & I (personally) have a view the suppliers in market are losing the appetite to provide loss leading plans when people churn away.
You also have a lot of players simply reselling another providers L3 service, which leaves very few commercial levers at their disposal.
These plans aren’t for everyone, but if you look at our 25/10 plan at $48.99, it’s only a few $’s more than some of the promo pricing, so eventually the promo hopping will be for nothing? Anyway, interesting chat, I guess it’s a watch this space?
All the best though & thanks for your feedback.
[M00Cow] So how much for a 500/50 or 1000/50 service with a static IP?
[Team Triforce] @M00Cow it’s an extra $5 p/Month for a static IP.
[Ezekiel2320] I was going to just make this comment:
"Mate as a recent customer, you still sound like a dick. Chill with the aggressive responses, it's not a good look"
But amusingly I'm actually having network issues as we speak 😆
Ookla speed tests with extreme pings and 30Mbps on my 500Mbps plan, but over 200Mbps when testing against www.ozspeedtest.com so 🤷
[askbargain] How many unplanned outages emails have you got recently?
[Wiadro] i havent been a customer for nearly a year and still get them.
[Team Triforce] The “unplanned interruptions” which cause a 5-minute “outage” while we redirect your traffic to a seperate gateway allow us to expand the network.
In most cases, these would result in 2-3 dropped pings, which most carriers do, without notifying customers.
We are trying to provide transparency & also ensuring these works are completed after hours, to minimise impact.
[Ezekiel2320] Zero emails since "your service has been activated"
[Team Triforce] Hasn’t been a maintenance window for a while… but it’s an inevitable part of managing a growing network.
We are talking 2-3 ping drops & extend latency while we route you through another POP.
If we did not advise customers, 99.9% wouldn’t even notice… but we are aiming to be transparent. This is all detailed & explained in the email communication too.
[Team Triforce] Log a ticket & I am happy to escalate & help! Send me a DM & will see what we can do to.
[Winny182] Having a good laugh reading all of OPs responses. Anyway I will continue to pay way less than this per month and not get smart ass replies from provider.
[Team Triforce] If you have a genuine question, I’m here to help! Little tired of the forum trolls, especially when they don’t make any sense!
[Hirolol] Good deal
Will sign my mum up

Also do you guys provision services over the weekend?
Can I sign up on the weekend, if so how long does it take?
[Team Triforce] Hmm… we can enable it for multiple?
Provisioning is automatic, assuming you provide a valid AVC ID.
If the provision goes as planned, the process takes 8-10 minutes, on some occasions it does fail & requires manual intervention.
[Wiadro] @Team Triforce:
the process takes 8-10 minutes, on some occasions it does fail & requires manual intervention.
manual intervention = 2 hours on the phone with someone who has no idea wtf is going on.
the process takes about 2 minutes if that, when the ISP is good.
[Team Triforce] @Wiadro: Wrong again… check the standard API times for a churn with the NBN.
At times, we acknowledge the call delays have been extended, a lot of time is spent helping users configure their own BYO routers, but the team has grown & this is no longer an issue.
[Wiadro] @Team Triforce:
Stage
Time frame

I've literally churned probably over a dozen times; it has generally been back online after I go to the toilet during a nervous new ISP week. So, under 3 minutes from the time I pressed confirm/submit on the website.
[Team Triforce] @Wiadro: Yes… the order is received, AVC ID’s are verified & then an order is queued for processing.
There are certain checks & balances, before the order is pushed to the NBN. This process does take some time, which is why we say 8-10 minutes as the time to complete.

Cheers!
[Team Triforce] I’m awake & responding… marketing all millennials! We will have it sorted first thing tomorrow… sorry!
Team just relaunched the new site design, been a long week!!
[Shaun Ross] Interesting post I have been a customer since the very beginning and after reading other people who have left comments.
I have been having my NBN drop out I was thinking it was something I done wrong I have disconnected all my house and reset everything and it still drops out. I have been getting billing problems too. Over charging for months then getting 7 refunds then told I am in arrears and having to pay 3 months.At first I found the very friendly but the last conversation I was being told I was wrong and they were right. So I am looking for a new NBN
Provider sometimes it's worth paying a little more to get better customers service when things go wrong.
[Team Triforce] Hi @Shaun Ross, this sounds like a genuine case of a bad experience! We don’t always get it right & we have had some challenges with the external billing provider we initially engaged.
This is all back in house now, so it should be much smoother… drop me a DM with your ticket # & I’ll happily step in to make sure we give you some compensation for the hassle.
Sincere apologies!

So I also would be grateful to buy 3. In fact I do believe I got a email two weeks ago telling me about the eero's but was about to change so didn't take it up. But I do appreciate someone telling it as it is. I don't want to change I was just fed up with being told I was sent invoice when I wasn't but I did when I was paying twice.
With luck I will be getting a new invoice soon.

Best regards Shaun
